recipes.name: Chef John's Chicken Cacciatore
ingredients_raw: 1 whole roasting chicken, cut in quarters
0.5 teaspoon red pepper flakes, or to taste
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat; add chicken and cook until browned on the outside. Remove to a bowl to capture the juices.
Stir in onions and mushrooms; cook for 5-6 minutes until soft. Add a big pinch of salt and pepper. Stir in garlic, rosemary, red pepper flakes, oregano, tomato sauce, and water.
Place chicken pieces and any juices that have accumulated in the bowl on top of the cooked vegetables. Add more salt and pepper. Place pepper slices on top of the chicken.
Cover and cook in the preheated oven for 1 hour 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Chef John's Chicken Cacciatore
raw_recipe.description: This simple Italian dish is packed with chicken, peppers, mushrooms and herbs for a satisfying one pot meal.

review.reviewBody:
I will usually never try a recipe unless there are pages of reviews but I was in the mood for this dish so I decided to go for it. I was NOT disappointed! The only thing I will change next time is to spice it up
A bit. Maybe season the chicken with some adobo before browning and add a bit more salt and pepper to the sauce. It wasn't bland but It was "mild". If you are like me and need tons of flavor then add some extra spices otherwise the dish is delicious as is.

My family LOVES this recipe! I made a few simple changes, nothing major. I used 3lbs of boneless thigh filets instead of a whole chicken, used a red onion, went a little heavy on the garlic, added 4 (14.5 oz) cans of tomatoes: Roma tomato sauce, petite, stewed, and diced (with basil, garlic and olive oil). I love aged, fermented apple cider vinegars made by American Vinegar Works, so added 1 T of red wine vinegar. This really brings out the other flavors! I cooked this dish in a slow cooker on LOW for 8 hours (this one really has a low setting; no scorching!), the last hour adding fresh cut basil and parsley (did not have rosemary).Served over Angel Hair pasta with lots of fresh grated parmesan. This was PERFECT. The bell peppers were amazing and the chicken was delicious and tender. The sauce had a beautiful depth of flavor. My family went nuts for it! Will definitely be making this many times in the future; can't wait to try it out on guests :)

A few small changes: Since I'm cooking for two I used four bone-in thighs with skin rather than a whole chicken, and I reduced the quantities of other ingredients appropriately. Also since we have fresh thyme in our garden I added a couple of sprigs and since I had some chicken stock on hand I used that rather than water. I used canned diced tomatoes instead of homemade tomato sauce (forgive me!). And I don't think it mattered, but it was too hot in our house to cook in the oven, so I put the Dutch oven in the gas barbeque outside and tried to keep it at about 350F. According to my customer (my wife) it was excellent. I'll definitely do it again. Update: I've made it several times now, and it's always excellent. Last time I served it on polenta, and today on couscous, using left over marinara sauce. Delicious as always.

This recipe is a new family FAVORITE! Really easy to prepare, if not a little time consuming, but you can always prep ahead of time and ready to go come dinner. I didn't have a whole chicken available but I subbed skin-on chicken thighs and butterflied chicken breasts with a few drumsticks for good measure. Worked just fine for me. Also, I used a whole 15oz can of crushed tomatoes with another 15oz can of tomato sauce (not soup!); will explain why below. I have a picker eater to cook for so I substituted the crushed red pepper with ground paprika (for flavor, less heat) and also sliced up thick matchstick carrots about 3" long add added last with the peppers before placing the dutch oven in the the 350 oven. Added a slight sweet finish at the end of the chew and matched the peppers tenderness perfectly! Will defiantly make this again. I served mine over slightly toasted/steamed long grain jasmine rice (I liked the extra sauce added to compliment the absorption of the rice) with just a little tarragon and melted butter.. SO GOOD!

modified this a bit by using 1/4 cup sherry after onions, garlic and shrooms soft. added fresh basil, oregano, and 1/2 tbs ground chili peppers. simmered and reduced. added sauce, and large can crushed tomatoes. brought to boil. placed chicken with peppers and baked for 45 min, covered in mozzarella and baked for 15 more minutes. served over vegetable pasta. spice was just right, just enough heat to bring a bead on the forehead without sacrificing the flavor. a keeper of a recipe.

This was an easy dish to recreate in my kitchen. I did make an adjustment or two. I used skinless, boneless chicken thighs (8 of them)seasoned them with Mrs. Dash original and a light dusting of garlic powder, then put them in the frying pan (coated with EVOO) and let them brown on both sides. I removed them to a plate and added the onions, mushrooms, garlic, hot pepper flakes (only about 10), oregano and a pinch of salt (I omitted the rosemary, as I did not have any). I let this cook about 8 minutes and added the tomato sauce (with 2 chopped up plum tomatoes in it) and a full cup of low sodium chicken broth. I added back the chicken cutlets and laid the pepper strips on top of them. Since it is summertime and very warm, I opted cover the fryer and simmer the recipe on top of the stove, checking on it every 20 minutes to make sure nothing was sticking to the bottom of the pan. It came out yummy . I lowered the total fat content as there was no chicken skin, and yet it was tender and juicy because I used thighs and not breasts.

We just made this for a family dinner and everyone loved it! I used boneless chicken breasts for time saving and serving flexibility. We sautéed veggies and chicken in electric skillet then put everything in a cast iron Dutch oven with a can of basil seasoned crushed tomatoes and simmered on the stovetop rather than in the oven. We served with curly pasta-cavatappi-salad and crusty bread - It was delicious!

Really easy to follow and great flavor. I added more garlic and onion. I also added a can of tomato paste mixed with some pasta water when I took it out of the oven. I took out the chicken first so I could more easily incorporate it into the sauce. I will use more mushrooms next time.

Absolutely delicious! The only things I did differently was I seasoned the chicken with salt, pepper & garlic powder before browning. Instead of tomato sauce I used a large can of crushed tomatoes and also added a few glugs of white wine. Instead of putting in the oven I simmered the covered pan on the stove top for almost an hour. Served over rigatoni. My husband went crazy for it. Thanks Chef John! I'm going to be making this dish often.

I should have triedthe recipe, as written, but I always read the comments first and then decide if I want to tweak. I forgot to cut the onion on the lines, but still SO good. I had already dry brined my chicken 24 hrs., before I settled on this recipe, so I added no salt to the recipe, and dredged them in flour before browning. I DID use 1.5 tsp red pepper flakes, and 1.5 tsp ground Oregano, instead of dried Oregano, as we love full flavor.I also used 1 C chicken broth instead of water, and in addition to the 1 C tomato sauce, I added 1 can diced tomato for more sauce. Lastly, I only used 3 Orange/Red peppers (green give me heartburn) AND the match book cut carrots another person suggested.Checked the chicken 1/4's at 1 hr. not ready and at 1 hr 15 min. the chicken was done and SOO juicy. Husband loved the flavors, peppers & onions, with carrot sweetness & pepper flakes.Next time I'll garnish with fresh basil or parsley from the garden, but this time we grated fresh parmesan on top for the last 10 minutes of baking and it was FANTASTIC next to the thin pasta we just brought home from Rome! Cheers and Enjoy!!
Great recipe - doubled the spices for extra flavor; used crushed tomatoes instead of tomato sauce and water.
I substituted white wine for the water. Next time I will work to make sauce thicker. Doubled the oregano.
Followed the recipe exactly with excellent results. I will most certainly make it again.
I floured the chicken before browning. Deglazed the pan with red wine and used homemade chicken stock, added fresh cherry tomatoes, fresh parsley and basil. I was delicious and the sauce was rich.
This was good, I just need to remember to add enough salt.
Excellent recipe. Even my husband liked it!
Boiled whole chicken In oven about 30 minutes
This was great as described. I might double the sauce to cook with rice.
